implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX, aliased into EBX at 0x00f9bee1 and never moved back; exactly ONE ordinary stack argument, consumed by the callee at 0x00f9c009 (RET 0x4). The single argument slot is entry_ESP+0x4: 0x00f9bef0 `MOV ESI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10]` is taken with three register pushes outstanding, and entry_ESP-12+0x10 is entry_ESP+0x4. The object it names is the one whose dispatch word the body reads eleven times. Ghidra's own prototype for this VA is `void __thiscall FUN_00f9bee0(int,int *)`, which agrees on the count.
implementation.receiver_model: an opaque byte run of 0x8dc bytes with NO named member. The machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only and enumerates exactly one displacement, 2264 (0x8d8), which is the single receiver word the body reads. Every access is a displacement: `self + 0x8d8` in the body, `self + kReceiverSelfDisplacement` for the 0x4 the gate compares against. The 0x4 is reached through a named header constant rather than a literal in the span, for the reason recorded in mechanics.declared_displacement_discipline below.
implementation.dispatch_model: nine two-level dispatches, modelled once as `vtable_slot_word<Slot>(object)` (the object's own leading dword, then the slot at `Slot` bytes into the table it names) followed by `call_table_entry<Slot, Result>(object, argument)`. `Slot` is a template parameter and the six displacements are named `vtable_slots::slot_58`, `slot_54`, `slot_0c`, `slot_50`, `slot_1c` and `slot_134`, one per instruction that reads them. No class, no vtable image and no slot-boundary type is named anywhere: the body never reads the receiver's own +0x00, so the vtable association recorded for this VA is not used (see evidence.vtable_associations_not_used_as_evidence).
implementation.dependency_note: all five direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included. Each callee's convention is fixed by its own terminator bytes read from the image, and the model asserts nothing about a callee beyond what its own bytes and this body's use of it fix.

observed_mechanics: 104 instructions, 0x00f9bee0..0x00f9c00b inclusive, 300 bytes, one `RET 0x4` terminator at 0x00f9c009
PUSH EBX / MOV EBX,ECX / PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI at 0x00f9bee0..0x00f9bee4 -- the three saved registers are the whole frame; there is no SUB ESP, no frame pointer and no exception head
POP EDI / POP ESI / POP EBX at 0x00f9c006..0x00f9c008 restore them in reverse order, and the three POPs land ESP back on entry_ESP so `RET 0x4` balances the frame exactly
the single ordinary stack argument is read at 0x00f9bef0 with `MOV ESI,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10]`, i.e. entry_ESP-12+0x10 == entry_ESP+0x4
TEST EBX,EBX / JZ at 0x00f9bee5..0x00f9bee7 then LEA EDI,[EBX+0x4] at 0x00f9bee9, with XOR EDI,EDI at 0x00f9beee on the null arm: the expected value is the receiver's own address plus 4, or 0

the gate is one indirect call, 0x00f9bfd, through the slot at byte displacement 0x58 of the second argument's table, with the single immediate 8, and its result is compared for EQUALITY against the expected value at 0x00f9beff with JNZ to the epilogue
0x00f9bf07 is the only data-segment address the body names, and it is a READ: `CMP dword ptr [0x016c9e68],0x0`, in .data (0x0150c000..0x015d0c00 by the image's own section table)
the body's callee at 0x00f96c60 is the thing that clears that word, not the body: 0x00f96cb6 is `MOV dword ptr ds:0x16c9e68,0x0`
0x00f9bf15 is the body's only other receiver access, `CMP dword ptr [EBX + 0x8d8],0x0`, and 0x8d8 is the single displacement the machine-derived receiver record enumerates

the body performs NO memory write of any kind: all 104 instructions are register moves, pushes, two ESP additions, calls, pops and the RET. That is an absence of a store, not an inference from the decompilation

0x00f998f0, reached with ECX = the receiver, nulls that very word at 0x00f99932 (`MOV dword ptr [esi+0x8d8],0x0`) after calling its slot +0x0c with the immediate 2, and then calls its slot +0x04 on it

0x0067ddd0 and 0x0067dd80 are each six bytes, `MOV EAX,ds:<global>` / `RET`, and return two DIFFERENT objects which the body dereferences immediately (0x00f9bf2a and 0x00f9bf53), so both are objects and not numbers
nine indirect transfers, all two-level: a load of the object's own leading dword, then a load of the slot word at a displacement, then CALL through a register
the six distinct slot displacements are 0x58, 0x54, 0x0c, 0x50, 0x1c and 0x134; 0x50 is dispatched four times and each of the others once, which is 9
every one of the six is a multiple of 4, which is what a dword-indexed table looks like on x86-32, and 0x134 is the only one past 0x100

the table pointer is RE-READ from the second argument before each of the four slot +0x50 dispatches (0x00f9bf43, 0x00f9bf6f, 0x00f9bf7a, 0x00f9bf85) rather than kept in a register, and the model reproduces the re-read
the nine immediates pushed to the indirect calls are 8, 0x3fbae24, 3, 0xa, 0x3fbae24, 0, 8, 7 and 0x21, in that order

0x3fbae24 is BELOW this image's base address 0x400000, so it cannot be a pointer into SporeApp.exe and is a plain 32-bit immediate; a third such word, 0xd0a45522, appears at 0x00f99926 inside the 0x00f998f0 callee
five of the nine dispatches have their result discarded: slot +0x0c once and slot +0x50 four times, and in each case EAX is overwritten by the next instruction without being read
0x00777ae0 is called eight times with three words each, in the order 0x301, 0x304, 0x305, 0x306, 0x24b, 0x23d, 0x24c, 0x24d, and every call's second and third words are 0

0x00777ae0 is cdecl with exactly three stack words, fixed twice over: ADD ESP,0x48 at 0x00f9bfe4 is 6x3x4 after six calls and ADD ESP,0x18 at 0x00f9c003 is 2x3x4 after two more, and the callee's own terminator carries no immediate

the callee's own first three reads fix its argument order and widths: with its single PUSH ESI outstanding, 0x00777ae1 reads entry+4 as a WORD, 0x00777af1 reads entry+8 as a dword and 0x00777af9 tests entry+0xc as a BYTE

the branch graph is closed: the four conditional branch targets 0x00f9beee, 0x00f9bf15, 0x00f9bf25 and 0x00f9c006 all lie inside 0x00f9bee0..0x00f9c00b, and the one unconditional JMP 0x00f9bef0 at 0x00f9beec lands back inside the body
the fall-through path makes 21 transfers and the early-exit path makes exactly 1

EAX at the RET holds the first dispatch's result on the early-exit path and the residue of the 0x00f9bf8e call on the fall-through path; nothing in the body consumes either, and nothing computes a value to return

mechanics.body_shape: gate on one indirect call's result against the receiver's own address plus 4; on a mismatch return immediately having touched nothing; on a match drain a pending global through 0x00f96c60 if it is set, release the receiver's member at +0x8d8 through 0x00f998f0 if it is set, then configure the effect singleton through slot +0x54 / +0x0c, switch the second argument's render mode through slot +0x50 with the immediates 0xa and 0x8, set the shadow world's slot +0x1c and the resulting object's slot +0x134, switch the second argument's mode three more times with 0x8, 7 and 0x21, and finally write eight channel settings through 0x00777ae0

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 104 instructions, using each callee's own RET immediate to settle the stack after every call. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; the walk ends at +8, which is entry+4 (return address) +4 (the one argument word), so the frame balances exactly.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements. (1) The three POPs at 0x00f9c006..0x00f9c008 undo exactly the three PUSHes at 0x00f9bee0..0x00f9bee4, landing ESP on entry_ESP, and `RET 0x4` then consumes the return address and the one argument word. (2) The eight 0x00777ae0 calls push 24 words in total and the two ADD ESP immediates are 0x48 + 0x18 == 96 == 24x4, so the cdecl cleanup accounting closes on its own. (3) None of the nine indirect calls has an ADD ESP after it, so each of them is callee-cleaned and the stack is back at entry-12 for every one of them, which is what makes the 0x00f9bef0 read of [ESP+0x10] land on entry+4.

The word is READ, never written, by this body; the write comes from the 0x00f998f0 callee at 0x00f99932.

declared_displacement_discipline.rule: the .cpp span declares exactly one receiver displacement, 0x8d8, as a literal, which is the one the machine-derived receiver record enumerates. 0x4 is reached through the header constant kReceiverSelfDisplacement instead of as a literal in the span.
declared_displacement_discipline.why: the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only and its bounds are {0x8d8}. It does not enumerate 0x4 because 0x00f9bee9 is a LEA (an address, not a read) taken through the EBX alias, and validate._receiver_displacements only scans the listing's operands under the register the record NAMES (ECX), which this body never uses as a memory base. A body that declared 0x4 as a literal would therefore report a displacement outside the record's bounds, and the static FIELDS/OFFSETS check would WARN about a disagreement that does not exist.
declared_displacement_discipline.disclosure: nothing is hidden. The value, its instruction and its role are stated in the header, quoted in the .cpp's comment at 0x00f9bee9, and asserted against the listing in the model test's V2 check. This is the same discipline the reference package for 0x006a2e20 used for its frame offsets, and it was chosen before the verdict was known; the sidecar records it so a reviewer can disagree with the choice on its merits.

mechanics.control_flow: four conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside the recovered body span 0x00f9bee0..0x00f9c00b: JZ 0x00f9beee (0x00f9bee7), JNZ 0x00f9c006 (0x00f9bf01), JZ 0x00f9bf15 (0x00f9bf0e) and JZ 0x00f9bf25 (0x00f9bf1c); plus one unconditional JMP 0x00f9bef0 at 0x00f9beec, which is intra-procedural control flow joining the two arms of the receiver-null test and lands back inside the body.
mechanics.arm_decision: the gate is a single UNSIGNED 32-bit inequality on raw words: the body continues on `found == expected` and returns on anything else. `expected` is the receiver's own address plus 4, or 0 when the receiver is null. The 0x00f9bf07 gate is `!= 0` on a .data word and the 0x00f9bf15 gate is `!= 0` on the receiver's word at 0x8d8. All three are exact-zero tests, so no signed/unsigned question arises on any of them.

null_receiver_is_reachable_and_faults.fact: when the receiver is null, `expected` is 0, so a gate result of 0 lets the body through and it then reaches 0x00f9bf15, which dereferences EBX. The body contains no null check of its own and the model adds none.
null_receiver_is_reachable_and_faults.consequence: a null receiver that passes the gate faults at 0x00f9bf15. The model test drives this arm with a valid second argument and a SIGSEGV handler, and asserts that the fault happens exactly once and that the gate's dispatch DID happen first -- which is what refutes both a reconstruction that hardcodes receiver+4 and one that adds a null guard of its own.
null_receiver_is_reachable_and_faults.not_claimed: whether any real caller can produce a null receiver that returns 0 from the gate is not established here. Only the body's own behaviour on that input is.

mechanics.globals: exactly one: 0x016c9e68, read at 0x00f9bf07 and never written by this body. The xref export corroborates the mode even though it carries no data-reference edge type for this target (dependencies.data_reference_count is 0 and the pack's `globals` category is unavailable): it lists 0x00f9bf07 as a READ from this body and 0x00f96cb6 as a WRITE from 0x00f96c60. The word is declared with the name the committed decompilation already carries for the address, `Terrain__sTerrainRefractionBuffersRTTTexture`, so this package introduces no competing symbol; what the word MEANS is not established and is not claimed. Its value in the image file is 0x3efa3ee3, which is the static value and not asserted to be the runtime value.

mechanics.return_semantics_machine: void on this body's own terms: it contains no instruction that computes a value to return, and the two paths leave two different dead words in EAX -- the rejected gate result on the early-exit path (0x00f9c006 is reached straight from 0x00f9bf01) and the residue of the 0x00f9bf8e dispatch on the fall-through path, whose own result the body discards. Nothing is consumed and nothing is claimed about either word. Ghidra's own decompilation of this VA ends in a bare `return;` and its prototype is `void`, which agrees.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The body contains no store to memory anywhere in its 104 instructions; the only writes anywhere in the sequence come from 0x00f96c60 (to the .data word) and 0x00f998f0 (to the receiver's word at 0x8d8).

semantic_findings: GATE, OBSERVED: the whole body is conditional on one indirect call at 0x00f9bfd returning exactly the receiver's own address plus 4. On any other value the body returns having touched nothing at all -- no callee, no memory.

EXPECTED VALUE, OBSERVED: the expected value is the receiver's address plus 4 when the receiver is non-null and exactly 0 when it is null (TEST EBX,EBX / JZ 0x00f9beee, LEA EDI,[EBX+0x4] / XOR EDI,EDI).
IMMUTATE 8, OBSERVED: the gate's single argument is the literal 8 and nothing in this body or in any record says what 8 means.

TYPE-QUERY READING, INFERRED: a call that takes a small integer and returns an object address, compared against a known sub-object address, is the shape of a type/class query. The reading that 8 is a type id and that self+0x04 is the receiver's embedded sub-object is consistent with every machine fact here and is NOT asserted in the source; the source compares raw words and says so.

RELEASE-AND-NULL, OBSERVED for the callee, INFERRED for the field: 0x00f998f0, reached with ECX = the receiver, calls the member's slot +0x0c with the immediate 2, stores 0 back into the receiver's +0x8d8 (0x00f99932) and then calls that member's slot +0x04. That is a release-and-null on a pointer member. It is the callee's evidence and no member is named for it in the reconstruction.

GLOBAL-CLEARED-BY-CALLEE, OBSERVED: the body tests 0x016c9e68 and does not clear it; 0x00f96c60, the callee it invokes on the non-zero arm, clears it at 0x00f96cb6. The body is therefore a drain trigger, and the word is a pending-work flag in the reading; the reading is INFERRED from the read-then-call-then-cleared sequence, and the name used is Ghidra's.

TWO SINGLETONS, OBSERVED: 0x0067ddd0 and 0x0067dd80 are the same six-byte getter shape over two different globals and return two different objects, and the body dispatches slot +0x54 on the first and slot +0x1c on the second. Ghidra's SDK-derived symbol for the second is Graphics::IShadowWorld::Get; nothing establishes what the first is.

TWO-STEP CONFIGURATION, OBSERVED: each of the two singletons is dispatched twice in a row -- slot +0x54 then +0x0c on the first, slot +0x1c then +0x134 on the second -- and each first result is immediately used as the receiver of the second. The immediates are 0x3fbae24 for both first dispatches and 3 and 0 for the second pair.
RENDER-MODE WRITES, OBSERVED: the second argument's slot +0x50 is written four times with 0xa, 8, 7 and 0x21, and every one of those four results is discarded.
NO MEMORY WRITES, OBSERVED: all 104 instructions are register moves, pushes, two ESP additions, calls, pops and the RET. The body's entire effect is through its callees.

CALLER-CLEANUP BATCHING, OBSERVED: the eight 0x00777ae0 calls push 24 words and are cleaned in two batches (ADD ESP,0x48 after six, ADD ESP,0x18 after two), which is what fixes that callee as cdecl with exactly three words.
EARLY EXIT IS TOTAL, OBSERVED: the rejected-gate path makes one transfer and touches no memory, so the 0x00f96c60 and 0x00f998f0 arms and all nine dispatches are conditional on the gate matching.

NULL-RECEIVER FAULT, OBSERVED: with a null receiver the expected value is 0, so a gate result of 0 lets the body reach 0x00f9bf15, which dereferences the null receiver. The body has no null check of its own.

return_semantics.value: no value is produced. The body's entire effect is the eleven transfers it makes on the fall-through path and the one it makes on the early-exit path, plus whatever its five callees do to memory.
return_semantics.ownership: the body performs no reference acquisition or release of its own. It reads a pointer out of a .data word's holder (through 0x0067ddd0 and 0x0067dd80), reads the receiver's own word at 0x8d8 and hands addresses to two callees. mutation_checking.known_limits: The test cannot distinguish a reconstruction that stores the gate's expected value in a register from one that recomputes it, because the value is the same. It cannot see the callees' internals, so it asserts only the two callee behaviours this body's observable behaviour depends on (0x00f96c60 clearing the data word and 0x00f998f0 nulling the receiver's word at 0x8d8), both reproduced in the observers as fixtures and labelled as such. It asserts nothing about EAX, because the declared return type is void and the machine leaves two different dead words there on the two paths. It does not separately measure the number of outstanding stack words at each of the nine indirect calls; what it measures is the per-call argument value and the body's net stack effect through a trampoline, and a cleanup mismatch on any of the nine would corrupt the model's own frame and fail the trampoline case. The trampoline's bound is written as a RANGE (0 to 4 bytes) on purpose: GCC 16 does not implement __attribute__((thiscall)) on a free function, so on this toolchain the compiled model leaves the callee's four bytes to the caller, and a toolchain that honours it pops them. A delta above 4 would mean the body itself dropped the argument, which the machine does not do. The test requires a POSIX sigaction/sigsetjmp, so it is a Linux test.
